name: Christiana Madu
text:
FreelancersOS was amazing!

What I learnt? got clarifications on what a skill is and tips on how to choose a skill to learn, stackable skills and all.

Something that shifted in my mindset? I saw  that young people were doing great things, eg, Faye, Mandy and some persons I connected with and I can be one of them and that was the shift in my mindset.

What stood out to me was the ease in the whole process, from the communication on WhatsApp to the main event on X, also this was the first time I joined a networking group without getting harassed by any of the guys, this was something I observed later, I don’t if the team filtered the members in the group but I noticed it and it’s worth mentioning.

What challenged me? Not exactly a challenge but an inspiration to do more, I mean if people can be achieving all these things in Tinubu’s Nigeria then I have no excuse.
I was glad I saw the link on Mandy’s status and clicked on it.

name: Faye
text:
A very big thank you to the convener of this event, Mandy Chinedum 〽️

Honestly… I’m still processing tonight.

I first entered FreelancersOS as an attendee.
Then I joined the team as the Communication Specialist.
And tonight, I hosted as the MC.

All of that happened in less than two weeks.

And truly, that in itself is a story to tell, to share, and to own.

Thank you so much, Mandy, for the labour and the body of work you shared tonight. The session was rich, layered, practical, and deeply reflective.

One thing I especially appreciated was the progression of the teaching. It felt like moving from one depth to another — almost like being led gradually into understanding.

From Mind OS…
to Skill OS…
to the introduction of Brand OS…

Everything connected.

And personally, tonight means a lot to me for another reason too.

This was the largest virtual space I have ever hosted as an MC and public speaker — over 35,000+ people live.

That alone stretched me.

But beyond that, tonight also became my first real execution step.

May 2025, I started building my service packages and brand structure as a communication strategist. Then, I didn't know it was a thing. I started by trying to understand how my skills connected:
writing,
communication,
brand thinking,
structure,
strategy…

I knew I could see patterns in communication, but I did not yet see how big it could be until this year.

Now I see clearer.

And, I have structure and strategy to work with thanks to the FreelancersOS.

Tonight, I also got to see how being a certified public speaker and MC adds to my skill stack.

That means a lot to me.

Thank you again to you, Mandy.

🌸

name: Isreal
text:
FreelancersOS gave me a clearer way to run my freelance work like a business. On Day 1, the point that a task-doer will burn while a CEO will scale changed how I look at my own work. The 4Ps roadmap (Proof, Positioning, Premium Output, Productization) and the reminder that talent alone isn't enough without structure gave me a practical path instead of just motivation.

Day 2 got even more practical. "Positioning is your sales catalyst" showed me that how clients understand what I do matters as much as the work itself. "If you want to serve kings, learn how to talk to kings" reminded me that communicating with higher-value clients is its own skill. And the idea that content strategy is a personal tactic, and that your content is your superpower, made me realize I don't need to copy anyone's style. I need to make mine work for me.
I'd recommend FreelancersOS to any freelancer who wants structure, not just inspiration.

name: Oluwaseyifunmi Precious OLADEJI
text:
FreelancersOS for me was great. I learnt a whole lot such as layers of mindset, principles of skills, the layers of positioning and the categories of skill.
What stood out for me was "Confidence is not just a feeling" and "Never dwell in the colony of your skills".
What challenged me is to do more. Every of the speakers inspired me and everything I learnt for that two days also inspired me.

name: Gabriel Addo
text:
FreelancersOS is one of the best virtual events I’ve attended. Everything was well -organized.
One of my biggest takeaways was learning to see my skill as not just talent, but as a business. It shifted my mindset from simply being a designer to thinking and operating more like a business owner.

What stood out for me the most was the realization that talent alone is not enough. You can have the skill, but knowing how to position yourself, execute, make decisions, and build a business around that skill is a must learn for every freelancer.

One thing that challenged me was realizing how much there is still to learn and put into practice. But that also became one of the things that inspired me.
My biggest takeaway? Is Execution will teach you things that learning alone never will. FreelancersOS reminded me that you don't just need to keep learning, but you need to take what you learn and actually put it into action.

name: Iroh Munachimso Peace
text:
FreelancerOS was a meeting I never expected would be the way it was, starting from the streaming to the mindset engineering.

One thing that has stayed me with for the longest is the fact that I realized that freelance is a business and not a just someone I do to make money. That has stayed with me. And each day i think of how to get better.

name: Great Tonyvoke
text:
FreelancersOS changed the way I think about my skill and what I can build with it.

Learning the five core areas, Skill OS, Client OS, Money OS, Brand OS, and Execution OS, helped me understand how everything connects. Before, I saw my skill more as something I could use as a side hustle. Now, I see it as something I can build a real business around.

What challenged me was realizing that being good at my skill is not enough. I have to think beyond the skill itself and learn how to build systems, understand clients, manage money, build my brand, and execute properly. What inspired me was seeing how these areas can come together to help me use my skill to solve real problems and build something sustainable.
